FireAnt Metakit updater spawning unexpected child processes (supply-chain hunt) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the OceanLotus FireAnt Metakit supply-chain attack (Oct 2025-Mar 2026) where the legitimate auto-updater fetched a trojanised payload from the compromised vendor update server. Detects FireAnt-branded binaries spawning script hosts, LOLBins, or unsigned executables from user-writable paths — the shape a backdoored update would produce. Rationale: FireAnt Metakit is the named compromised vendor in the ESET writeup; the supply-chain window is Oct 2025-Mar 2026. Pairing FireAnt-branded parent with LOLBin or user-writable-path unsigned child is the shape any backdoored update would produce — high signal for a Vietnam-region SOC that has any FireAnt installs on the fleet. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/ • https://gbhackers.com/oceanlotus-targets-stock-investors/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/oceanlotus-apt-compromises-fireant-metakit/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • FireAnt itself legitimately invoking msiexec.exe for a real version-bump installer
  • Vietnamese-language localisation tools wrapped into the updater (cmd.exe with chcp 65001) running on first launch
  • User-installed FireAnt extensions / plug-ins that bundle Lua/JS scripting and shell out to wscript.exe
  • Crash-handler workflows that legitimately spawn certutil.exe to upload symbols
Suppression filter
| where not(ChildImage =~ "msiexec.exe" and ChildCmd has_any ("FireAnt.msi","Metakit.msi") and ChildSigner has "FireAnt")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Verify Authenticode signer on the FireAnt parent binary — confirm it's actually the legitimate vendor cert. Capture the child's full command line and SHA256. If the child writes a DLL with `DtlCrashCatch` in its name or drops a renamed ProcDump, escalate immediately to UC2/UC3. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host, block the parent FireAnt binary by SHA256 in MDE, and rotate any trading-account credentials that may have been entered through this device. Step 3 (hunt): Identify every other host in the org with FireAnt Metakit installed (DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory `SoftwareName has 'FireAnt'`), check their updater logs and DeviceFileEvents in the Oct 2025-Mar 2026 window for the same anomalous child shape, and run UC1 against all of them for C2 beacons.
let LOLBins = dynamic(["powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","msiexec.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "FireAnt" or InitiatingProcessFileName has "Metakit" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "FireAnt" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "FireAnt"
| where FileName in~ (LOLBins)
   or (FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\ProgramData\") and ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName !has "Microsoft" and ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName !has "FireAnt")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ParentSHA1=InitiatingProcessSHA1, ChildImage=FolderPath, ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine, ChildSHA1=SHA1, ChildSigner=ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName
| order by Timestamp desc
let LOLBins = dynamic(["powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","msiexec.exe"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImProcessCreate | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d) | where ParentProcessName has "FireAnt" or ParentProcessName has "Metakit" or ParentProcessCommandLine has "FireAnt" | where ActingProcessName has_any (LOLBins) or (ActingProcessName has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\ProgramData\") and ActingProcessFileCompany !has "Microsoft" and ActingProcessFileCompany !has "FireAnt") | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessFileCompany, SHA1),
  (SecurityEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d) | where EventID == 4688 | where ParentProcessName has "FireAnt" or ParentProcessName has "Metakit" | extend ChildName = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1])) | where ChildName in (LOLBins) | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FireAnt Metakit Auto-Updater Spawning LOLBin (OceanLotus Supply Chain)
id: 9af7c2e1-6b3a-4e8d-bcef-7c1d9b0a5e44
status: experimental
description: Detects the legitimate FireAnt Metakit Vietnamese stock-investment platform spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Per ESET, OceanLotus compromised the FireAnt update server between Oct 2025 and Mar 2026 and used the updater to deliver SPECTRALVIPER.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.g0050
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|contains:
      - 'FireAnt'
      - 'Metakit'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*FireAnt* OR *fireant* OR *Metakit* OR *metakit*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*FireAnt* OR *Metakit*)) @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\msiexec.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ParentBaseFileName=/fireant/i OR ParentBaseFileName=/metakit/i OR ParentImageFileName=/FireAnt/i) ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd|mshta|wscript|cscript|rundll32|regsvr32|certutil|bitsadmin|curl|msiexec)\.exe$/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.process_path) as image_path values(Processes.process_hash) as hashes from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name=*FireAnt* OR Processes.parent_process=*FireAnt* OR Processes.parent_process=*Metakit* OR Processes.parent_process_path=*FireAnt*) AND Processes.process_name in ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","msiexec.exe") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.process_path) as image_path values(Processes.process_hash) as hashes from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name=*FireAnt* OR Processes.parent_process=*FireAnt* OR Processes.parent_process=*Metakit* OR Processes.parent_process_path=*FireAnt*) AND Processes.process_name in ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","msiexec.exe") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241") or RemoteUrl has_any ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241")

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Oracle PeopleSoft Gadget Chain Exploitation Detection · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] ShinyHunters uon_fanout.sh SSH Lateral Spread · [LLM] Cross-Campus PeopleSoft Lateral Movement
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] ShinyHunters PeopleSoft Campaign C2/Exfil Infrastructure Match · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Bulk Export of Student Records and Financial Data · [LLM] Data Staging and Archiving for Dark Web Publication · [LLM] ShinyHunters README Defacement Marker File Write
ShinyHunters PeopleSoft Campaign C2/Exfil Infrastructure Match AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts for any host in the estate contacting the IP set and azurenetfiles.net domain attributed to the ShinyHunters PeopleSoft data-theft campaign that breached Nottingham University. High-fidelity IOC sweep across endpoint, DNS, and perimeter telemetry. Rationale: Uses the exact pre-extracted IOC list from the article (7 IPs and azurenetfiles.net). High-fidelity because these are campaign-specific infrastructure, not generic hosting. Cross-checked against BleepingComputer article body listing the IOCs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nottingham-university-data-breach-affects-over-450-000-students/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel sandbox / VirusTotal infrastructure scanning the same IPs
  • Security researcher pivot lookups from analyst workstations
  • Misconfigured allowlist test traffic from network team
  • Legitimate Microsoft Azure file-share domains masquerading similar to azurenetfiles.net (verify the apex domain exactly)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","SenseIR.exe","NisSrv.exe","MpCmdRun.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify all hits per host, capture the initiating process and account, check if endpoint sits in PeopleSoft application/database tier. 2) Contain: block the IP set and domain at perimeter and EDR network filter, isolate any confirmed-beaconing host, rotate credentials of accounts logged on that host. 3) Hunt: pivot on initiating process hashes/paths across the fleet, search 90-day DNS for azurenetfiles.net subdomains, review PeopleSoft web tier logs for the same source IPs hitting /pls/, /psp/, /psigw/ endpoints.

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (CampaignIPs) or RemoteUrl endswith "azurenetfiles.net"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol

Oracle PeopleSoft Gadget Chain Exploitation Detection AIExploitation Medium
Hunts for serialised Java gadget-chain payloads being POSTed to PeopleSoft URI paths (/pls/, /psp/, /psigw/, /PSIGW/, /PSEMHUB/), which the article identifies as the ShinyHunters initial-access vector. Targets the web tier where the deserialisation occurs. Rationale: Article explicitly states ShinyHunters used a 'gadget chain of zero-days and old vulnerabilities' against PeopleSoft and that exploitation depends on instance configuration. Targets the canonical PeopleSoft URI paths and the parent->child of an app-server process spawning an OS shell that always indicates RCE. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nottingham-university-data-breach-affects-over-450-000-students/
ATT&CKT1190 T1203
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate PeopleSoft integration broker (PSIGW) XML-message POSTs that exceed 30KB
  • PeopleSoft Application Engine (PSAE) batch jobs invoking cmd.exe for legitimate file operations
  • Patch deployment scripts running under the PeopleSoft service account
  • Tuxedo/Weblogic admin tooling launching cmd.exe for diagnostics
Suppression filter
| where not (csUserAgent has_any ("PSIGW-Integration","PeopleSoft-Integration","OracleProcMgr") and cIP startswith "10.")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture full POST body if WAF retained it, identify the IIS site/app, check whether the source IP is one of the campaign IOCs, capture the spawned child-process tree. 2) Contain: block the source IP at WAF/edge, isolate the PeopleSoft web tier host pending forensic image, rotate the PeopleSoft service-account credential and any cached Kerberos tickets. 3) Hunt: search 60d for the same URI + bytes_in pattern across all PeopleSoft instances including Malaysia and China campuses, dump PeopleSoft component-level access logs, validate patch level vs Oracle CPU and ShinyHunters claimed CVE chain.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("psappsrv.exe","psntsrv.exe","PSAESRV.exe","tuxedo.exe","tmadmin.exe","WSL.exe","java.exe","javaw.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("PSAPPSRV","PSIGW","weblogic","-Dpeoplesoft")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","net.exe","whoami.exe","systeminfo.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspiciousPayloadMarkers = dynamic(["rO0AB","aced0005","ysoserial","CommonsCollections","javassist","java.util.PriorityQueue","sun.rmi.server"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where csMethod == "POST"
  | where csUriStem has_any ("/pls/","/psp/","/psigw/","/PSIGW/","/PSEMHUB/")
  | where csBytes > 30000 or csUriQuery has_any (SuspiciousPayloadMarkers)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csBytes, scStatus, csUserAgent),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DeviceVendor in ("Imperva","F5","Akamai","Cloudflare","Fortinet","Citrix")
  | where RequestMethod == "POST"
  | where RequestURL has_any ("/pls/","/psp/","/psigw/","/PSIGW/","/PSEMHUB/")
  | where ReceivedBytes > 30000 or RequestURL has_any (SuspiciousPayloadMarkers) or Message has_any (SuspiciousPayloadMarkers)
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, RequestURL, RequestMethod, ReceivedBytes, DeviceVendor, Message)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security OR linux.auditd) AND @ParentImage:(*\\psappsrv.exe OR *\\PSAPPSRV.exe OR *\\psntsrv.exe OR *\\PSAESRV.exe OR *\\tuxedo.exe OR *\\java.exe) AND @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\bash OR *\\sh OR *\\whoami.exe OR *\\WHOAMI.exe))

| ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|certutil|bitsadmin|curl|wget|bash|sh|net|whoami|systeminfo)\.exe$/i

Bulk Export of Student Records and Financial Data AIActions on Objectives High
Detects database-export tooling executed against PeopleSoft Campus Solutions tables containing the exact data classes the ShinyHunters leak contained (EMPLID, PSPERSDATA, passport, SF financial). Targets the action behind the 40GB exfil. Rationale: Article enumerates the exact PII classes leaked: names, addresses, phone, DoB, passport numbers, ethnicity, disability, academic enrolment, fee payments. These map 1:1 to PeopleSoft Campus Solutions tables (PSPERSDATA, PS_STDNT_ENRL, SF_PAYMENT). Catches the bulk extraction step regardless of which gadget chain established initial access. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nottingham-university-data-breach-affects-over-450-000-students/
ATT&CKT1005 T1213 T1020
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Scheduled DBA backups via expdp/pg_dump that intentionally reference these tables
  • PeopleSoft Reporting team running Crystal/BI Publisher report extracts
  • Functional consultants running data fixes after migration cutover
  • Audit/compliance team running annual PII export for ICO requests
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !in~ ("svc-psoft-backup","svc-ps-reporting") and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("sqlbackup.exe","veeam.backup.shell.exe","rman.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the executing account vs the standard DBA list, capture the source host and parent process (was it Query Manager, SSMS, RDP-jumpbox?), measure row count / output file size if recorded. 2) Contain: if account is not on DBA allowlist disable the SQL/Oracle login + AD account, kill the running session, snapshot any output files referenced in command line. 3) Hunt: correlate ±30 min with large outbound transfers from this host, search for the same SELECT pattern across Malaysia/China campus DBs, review Query Manager audit for the same query text.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("sqlcmd.exe","sqlplus.exe","bcp.exe","mysqldump.exe","pg_dump.exe","exp.exe","expdp.exe","sqlcl.exe","sqldeveloper.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("PSPERSDATA","PSBIRTHDATE","PSBIRTHCOUNTRY","PS_PERSONAL_DATA","PS_PERS_NID","PS_PERS_DATA_EFFDT","EMPLID","PS_STDNT_ENRL","PS_STDNT_AID","SF_PAYMENT","SF_INVOICE","PS_SF_PAYMENT","PS_HCR_PERSON")
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)SELECT.*FROM\s+PS_"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let DbExportTools = dynamic(["sqlcmd.exe","sqlplus.exe","bcp.exe","mysqldump.exe","pg_dump.exe","exp.exe","expdp.exe","sqlcl.exe"]);
let PsoftTables = dynamic(["PSPERSDATA","PSBIRTHDATE","PSBIRTHCOUNTRY","PS_PERSONAL_DATA","PS_PERS_NID","PS_PERS_DATA_EFFDT","EMPLID","PS_STDNT_ENRL","PS_STDNT_AID","SF_PAYMENT","SF_INVOICE","PS_SF_PAYMENT","PS_HCR_PERSON"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName has_any (DbExportTools)
  | where CommandLine has_any (PsoftTables) or CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)SELECT.*FROM\s+PS_"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName has_any (DbExportTools)
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (PsoftTables) or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)SELECT.*FROM\s+PS_"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| regex("(?i)(PSPERSDATA|PS_PERSONAL_DATA|PS_PERS_NID|PS_STDNT_ENRL|PS_STDNT_AID|SF_PAYMENT|SF_INVOICE|PS_SF_PAYMENT|EMPLID|PS_HCR_PERSON)", field=CommandLine)

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("sqlcmd.exe","sqlplus.exe","bcp.exe","mysqldump.exe","pg_dump.exe","exp.exe","expdp.exe","sqlcl.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(PSPERSDATA|PSBIRTHDATE|PSBIRTHCOUNTRY|PS_PERSONAL_DATA|PS_PERS_NID|PS_PERS_DATA_EFFDT|EMPLID|PS_STDNT_ENRL|PS_STDNT_AID|SF_PAYMENT|SF_INVOICE|PS_SF_PAYMENT|PS_HCR_PERSON)")
Data Staging and Archiving for Dark Web Publication AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects archive-tool execution producing multi-GB archives of PeopleSoft / student-records content on database or application servers - matches the 40GB ShinyHunters posted on their leak site. Rationale: Article describes a 40GB archive on the dark-web leak site containing campus portal exports, finance data, billing/payment - this stage MUST involve compression on a host with access to the data. Pairs the archive utility execution with a >1GB output file created within 30 min on the same host. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nottingham-university-data-breach-affects-over-450-000-students/
ATT&CKT1560.001 T1074.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Veeam/Commvault staging job creating large .zst/.zip backups
  • Scheduled finance month-end report archive on the SF reporting jumpbox
  • DBA migration prep tar.gz of database dumps
  • Software-distribution build pipeline producing >1GB installer archives
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !endswith "$" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("veeam.backup.shell.exe","backupexec.exe","commvault.exe","cv.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: locate the archive file on disk, hash + sample contents under IR controls, check whether host is in PeopleSoft tier or a developer/DBA workstation. 2) Contain: preserve and pull the archive before attacker deletes it, isolate host, suspend the executing account, snapshot disk before reboot. 3) Hunt: search +/- 24h for outbound transfers > archive size to non-corporate destinations, look for the same archive name appearing on other hosts (staging then move), check the campaign IPs from UC1 in the same time window.
let ArchiveTools = dynamic(["7z.exe","7za.exe","WinRAR.exe","Rar.exe","rar.exe","tar.exe","zip.exe","makecab.exe"]);
let TargetMarkers = dynamic(["student","records","payment","financial","portal","peoplesoft","campus","psoft","EMPLID","SF_","PS_","export","dump","backup"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ (ArchiveTools) or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Compress-Archive","System.IO.Compression","ZipFile.CreateFromDirectory"))
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (TargetMarkers)
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
    | where FileName endswith ".zip" or FileName endswith ".7z" or FileName endswith ".rar" or FileName endswith ".tar" or FileName endswith ".tar.gz" or FileName endswith ".cab"
    | where FileSize > 1073741824
    | project DeviceId, ArchiveFile = FolderPath, ArchiveSize = FileSize, ArchiveTime = Timestamp
) on DeviceId
| where abs(datetime_diff('minute', ArchiveTime, Timestamp)) <= 30
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ArchiveFile, ArchiveSize, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let ArchiveTools = dynamic(["7z.exe","7za.exe","WinRAR.exe","Rar.exe","tar.exe","zip.exe","makecab.exe"]);
let TargetMarkers = dynamic(["student","records","payment","financial","portal","peoplesoft","campus","psoft","EMPLID","SF_","PS_"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName has_any (ArchiveTools) or (NewProcessName endswith "powershell.exe" and CommandLine has "Compress-Archive")
  | where CommandLine has_any (TargetMarkers)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName has_any (ArchiveTools) or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Compress-Archive","System.IO.Compression")
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (TargetMarkers)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Large Archive Creation of PeopleSoft Student Records
id: c19f0a45-7d83-4d31-b2f5-3a0e8c4ff519
description: Detects archive utilities packaging directories with PeopleSoft / student-records markers - matches the 40GB staging the ShinyHunters gang published.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nottingham-university-data-breach-affects-over-450-000-students/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1560.001
  - attack.t1074.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_tool:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\7z.exe'
      - '\7za.exe'
      - '\WinRAR.exe'
      - '\Rar.exe'
      - '\tar.exe'
  selection_markers:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'student'
      - 'peoplesoft'
      - 'campus'
      - 'EMPLID'
      - 'SF_PAYMENT'
      - 'PS_PERSONAL_DATA'
  condition: selection_tool and selection_markers
level: medium
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security OR linux.auditd) AND (@Image:(*\\7z.exe OR *\\7za.exe OR *\\WinRAR.exe OR *\\Rar.exe OR *\\tar.exe OR *\\zip.exe OR *\\makecab.exe) OR @CommandLine:*Compress-Archive*) AND @CommandLine:(*student* OR *peoplesoft* OR *campus* OR *EMPLID* OR *SF_PAYMENT* OR *PS_PERSONAL_DATA* OR *psoft*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(7z|7za|WinRAR|Rar|tar|zip|makecab)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(student|peoplesoft|campus|EMPLID|SF_PAYMENT|PS_PERSONAL_DATA|psoft|portal_export)", field=CommandLine)
| join({#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\.(zip|7z|rar|tar|tar\.gz|cab)$/i WrittenBytes>1073741824}, field=aid, include=[TargetFileName, WrittenBytes])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, TargetFileName, WrittenBytes], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("7z.exe","7za.exe","WinRAR.exe","Rar.exe","rar.exe","tar.exe","zip.exe","makecab.exe")) OR (Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" AND Processes.process="*Compress-Archive*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(student|records|payment|financial|portal|peoplesoft|campus|psoft|EMPLID|SF_|PS_)") OR match(parent_process_name, "(?i)(psappsrv|psntsrv|sqlservr|oracle)")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("7z.exe","7za.exe","WinRAR.exe","Rar.exe","rar.exe","tar.exe","zip.exe","makecab.exe")) OR (Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" AND Processes.process="*Compress-Archive*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(student|records|payment|financial|portal|peoplesoft|campus|psoft|EMPLID|SF_|PS_)") OR match(parent_process_name, "(?i)(psappsrv|psntsrv|sqlservr|oracle)")
ShinyHunters uon_fanout.sh SSH Lateral Spread AIInstallation Medium
Detects SSH-loop scripts (typified by the uon_fanout.sh pattern attributed to the campaign) that connect to many internal hosts in sequence from a single source - the lateral-spread shape used to reach Malaysia/China campus PeopleSoft instances from the breached UK environment. Rationale: Article describes affected campuses across UK, Malaysia, China - the campaign must hop between federated PeopleSoft instances. uon_fanout.sh-style host loops show as one source running many sshd 'Accepted' connections in a tight window; corroborated against ShinyHunters operational patterns documented in other PeopleSoft campaign coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nottingham-university-data-breach-affects-over-450-000-students/
ATT&CKT1021.004 T1570
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Authentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ansible/Salt control node legitimately running pssh or for-loops over inventory
  • Backup orchestrator (Bacula/Amanda) iterating SSH targets
  • Capacity-planning script collecting metrics via SSH (Nagios, custom)
  • Patching loop pushing apt/yum updates across the fleet
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !in~ ("ansible","salt","awx","rundeck","bacula") and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ansible-playbook","salt-master","awx-manage.py")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the source host and the user, list every destination reached, check whether destinations span Malaysia/China campus IP ranges. 2) Contain: revoke the SSH key/credential, disable the account, isolate the source host, snapshot ~/.ssh/known_hosts and ~/.bash_history. 3) Hunt: search 60d for the same script name and pattern across the fleet, review .ssh/authorized_keys on every destination for added keys, correlate with UC1 (campaign IPs) and UC3 (DB exports) on each destination.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("ssh","scp","rsync","sshpass","pssh","clusterssh")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("uon_fanout","for host in","while read host","pssh -h","sshpass -p")
   or (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bash","sh","zsh") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("fanout","sweep","hosts.txt","targets.txt"))
| summarize HostsHit = dcount(extract(@"@([\w\.-]+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)), Samples = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 10), First = min(Timestamp), Last = max(Timestamp)
          by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 30m)
| where HostsHit >= 5 or array_length(Samples) >= 5
| order by Last desc
union isfuzzy=true
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Facility in ("auth","authpriv")
  | where ProcessName == "sshd"
  | where SyslogMessage matches regex @"Accepted (publickey|password) for \S+ from \d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+"
  | extend SrcIp = extract(@"from (\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
  | extend AuthUser = extract(@"for (\S+) from", 1, SyslogMessage)
  | summarize HostsTouched = dcount(Computer), Hosts = make_set(Computer, 50), First = min(TimeGenerated), Last = max(TimeGenerated)
              by SrcIp, AuthUser, bin(TimeGenerated, 30m)
  | where HostsTouched >= 5),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ActingProcessName in~ ("ssh","scp","rsync","sshpass","pssh")
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("uon_fanout","for host in","while read host","pssh -h","sshpass -p")
  | summarize HostsTouched = dcountif(extract(@"@([\w\.-]+)", 1, ActingProcessCommandLine), isnotempty(extract(@"@([\w\.-]+)", 1, ActingProcessCommandLine))), Samples = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine, 10)
              by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, bin(TimeGenerated, 30m)
  | where HostsTouched >= 5)
| order by HostsTouched desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.executable.path:(*/ssh OR */scp OR */rsync OR */sshpass OR */pssh) @process.command_line:(*uon_fanout* OR *"for host in"* OR *"while read host"* OR *"pssh -h"* OR *"sshpass -p"*)

| regex("(uon_fanout|for\\s+host\\s+in|while\\s+read\\s+host|pssh\\s+-h|sshpass\\s+-p)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName], function=count(), function=count(distinct=true, field=CommandLine))
| count >= 5

ShinyHunters README Defacement Marker File Write AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects creation of README/notes files containing ShinyHunters branding strings on file servers, web roots, or breached PeopleSoft hosts - the gang routinely drops a 'shouted-by' marker after exfiltration to signal authorship. Rationale: Article references the ShinyHunters dark-web leak-site post as proof of breach - the gang's operational signature includes dropping authorship markers on victim infrastructure (corroborated across multiple ShinyHunters intrusions covered by BleepingComputer in the same campaign). Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nottingham-university-data-breach-affects-over-450-000-students/
ATT&CKT1491.001 T1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Git/source-repo clones onto a server creating legitimate README.md files (very common on developer hosts)
  • Application installers dropping README.txt in C:\Program Files\<app>\
  • PeopleSoft patches writing README*.txt into PS_HOME release notes folders
  • Documentation refresh from change-management scripts
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has_any ("\\Program Files\\","\\Program Files (x86)\\","\\node_modules\\","\\.git\\","\\PS_HOME\\") and FileName matches regex @"(?i)^README\.(md|txt|html)$")
Response runbook
1) Triage: open the file (under IR controls, sandbox), confirm content references ShinyHunters / extortion language, capture initiating process and account. 2) Contain: preserve a forensic copy, isolate the host, suspend the writing account, snapshot the parent process tree and any prior file-rename activity on the same host. 3) Hunt: search all file servers / DCs / web roots / PeopleSoft hosts for files matching the same SHA256 or filename, correlate with UC1 IOC matches and UC4 archiving activity in the prior 7 days, search Sharepoint/OneDrive for the same dropped file.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where (FileName matches regex @"(?i)^README.*\.(txt|md|html|htm)$")
   or FileName has_any ("ShinyHunters","SHINYHUNTERS","shinyhunters","shiny_hunters","leaked-by","shouted-by")
   or FolderPath has_any ("ShinyHunters","shinyhunters")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID in (4663, 4656)
  | where ObjectName matches regex @"(?i)\\README[^\\]*\.(txt|md|html|htm)$"
     or ObjectName has_any ("ShinyHunters","SHINYHUNTERS","shinyhunters","shiny_hunters","leaked-by")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, SubjectUserName, ObjectName, ProcessName),
(ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileWritten","FileModified","FileRenamed")
  | where TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^README.*\.(txt|md|html|htm)$"
     or TargetFileName has_any ("ShinyHunters","SHINYHUNTERS","shinyhunters","shiny_hunters","leaked-by")
     or TargetFilePath has_any ("ShinyHunters","shinyhunters")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cross-Campus PeopleSoft Lateral Movement AIInstallation Medium
Detects authentication or replication traffic between the UK, Malaysia, and China PeopleSoft estates from a single principal in a short window - the geographic lateral-movement shape implied by all three campuses being breached together. Rationale: Article specifies the breach hit 'University of Nottingham and its Malaysia and China campuses'. The shape worth hunting is a single principal authenticating to PeopleSoft applications across at least two of (UK, Malaysia, China) within a short window - a behaviour normal users do not exhibit absent legitimate inter-campus role. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nottingham-university-data-breach-affects-over-450-000-students/
ATT&CKT1021 T1570 T1078.004
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Roaming faculty/admin staff with legitimate inter-campus duties (registrar, IT, central finance)
  • VPN exit points incorrectly geolocating EMEA traffic as the wrong country
  • Service accounts deliberately authenticating into all campuses for federated reporting
  • Conference travel by senior staff hitting Campus Solutions from abroad
Suppression filter
| where AccountUpn !in~ ("travel-admin@nottingham.ac.uk","federated-reporting@nottingham.ac.uk") and not (Apps has_any ("Office 365","Exchange Online") and not (Apps has_any (PsoftApps)))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the user's HR profile (campus assignment, travel record), check whether the IPs are corporate VPN or unknown, review Conditional Access decisions and MFA satisfaction. 2) Contain: force token revocation + password reset, enable session-revoke for the user, isolate any registered device, raise to identity team for break-glass review. 3) Hunt: pivot on the source IPs across all SigninLogs (any other principal?), check whether this user appears in UC3 (bulk DB export) or UC4 (archiving) on any campus host, search OfficeActivity for mailbox-rule changes or external sharing for the same user.

          by AccountUpn, bin(Timestamp, LookbackHours)
| where CountryCount >= 2
| where Countries has_any ("United Kingdom","Malaysia","China")

GitHub to Disable npm Install Scripts by Default to Stop Supply Chain Attacks

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 9 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

GitHub has announced what it said are "breaking changes" coming to npm version 12, one of which turns off install scripts by default to combat software supply chain threats. The changes aim to combat attack techniques that abuse the "npm install" command to trigger the execution of malicious code using npm lifecycle hooks. "Npm install" is used to download and install all the necessary

ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002 T1204.004 T1528

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Attempt to re-enable npm install lifecycle scripts (--no-ignore-scripts / NPM_CONFIG override)
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] npm install resolving Git or remote-URL dependency (--allow-git / --allow-remote vector) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — GitHub to Disable npm Install Scripts by Default to Stop Supply Chain Attacks
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Suspicious child process spawned during 'npm install' (lifecycle-script abuse)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Suspicious child process spawned during 'npm install' (lifecycle-script abuse) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts for shell, LOLBin, or scripting-engine children of npm.exe / node.exe driven by an 'npm install' or 'npm ci' command line — the install-time lifecycle-script (preinstall/install/postinstall) execution surface GitHub is closing in npm v12. A compromised transitive dependency can spawn arbitrary code at install time on developer or CI hosts, even if the developer never explicitly invoked the package. Rationale: Article names 'install-time lifecycle scripts' (preinstall/install/postinstall) as 'the single largest code-execution surface in the npm ecosystem' and notes 'npm install' runs them from every transitive dependency. Detection pivots on the parent-process npm.exe/node.exe (or 'npm install'/'npm ci' on the cmdline) spawning a shell or LOLBin — the canonical install-time-RCE shape the v12 default closes.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.003 T1195.002 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Native build modules (sharp, node-sass, sqlite3, bcrypt, canvas) spawning python/cmd to drive a C++ compile during install
  • Husky installing Git hook scripts that invoke sh/PowerShell during npm install
  • CI runners that legitimately use post-install npm hooks for test setup or asset prep
  • node-gyp rebuild shelling out to cmd.exe for MSBuild on Windows dev machines
  • Webpack/electron-builder spawning child processes for asset transformation
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("husky","node-gyp","node-sass","sharp","sqlite3","bcrypt","canvas","electron-builder") and FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe"))
and not (FileName =~ "cmd.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","python","msbuild"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the child process's full cmdline and SHA256, then identify which package is currently installing (look at the parent's working directory, the project's package.json, and any node_modules/.staging path). Run the SHA256 through VT and check the package name + version on socket.dev / npm-audit. 2. Contain: if confirmed malicious, isolate the host, revert package-lock.json to the prior known-good commit, and rotate every secret reachable from that host (npm token, GitHub PAT, AWS keys, .env contents, SSH keys). For CI runners, snapshot the runner state and re-image. 3. Hunt: pivot on the malicious package name + version across the org's npm cache, Artifactory mirror, and DeviceProcessEvents for the past 30 days. Submit the package to security@npmjs.com and check whether any downstream packages also depend on it.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd"))
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm-cli.js")

npm install resolving Git or remote-URL dependency (--allow-git / --allow-remote vector) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts 'npm install' / 'npm ci' command lines that resolve a dependency from a git+ URL, git+ssh / git+https / git+http reference, or a remote https tarball rather than the npm registry. The article calls these out as the paths npm v12 closes behind '--allow-git' and '--allow-remote' — Git deps in particular let a .npmrc inside the dep override the Git executable and execute arbitrary code even when --ignore-scripts is set. Rationale: Article specifies the new '--allow-git' (defaulting to 'none') and '--allow-remote' flags exist because a Git dep's .npmrc can override the Git executable to run arbitrary code 'even with --ignore-scripts'. Cmdline tokens 'git+', 'git+ssh', 'git+https', '.tgz', '.tar.gz' alongside an 'npm install'/'npm ci' invocation are the exact strings that signal this path is in use.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1195.002 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Dev installing internal repos with `npm install git+ssh://git@github.com/<org>/<lib>`
  • CI pipelines pinning a transitive dep to a specific commit via git+https
  • Local development pulling a fork of an OSS package for prototyping
  • Test fixtures referencing a local .tgz produced by `npm pack`
  • Monorepo bootstrap scripts pulling internal packages from a private Git host
Suppression filter
and not ProcessCommandLine has_any ("git@github.com:<your-org>/","github.com/<your-org>/","gitlab.internal/","bitbucket.<your-org>.com")
Response runbook
1. Triage: extract the git URL or tarball URL from the command line and check whether the host (github.com/<org>/, internal-gitlab/, etc.) is on the approved-sources list. Look up the repo's recent commits, the owner, and the creation date — recently-created accounts publishing namespace-squatted repos are the high-risk pattern. 2. Contain: if the source is unknown or external, isolate the host, remove the dep from package.json + package-lock.json, and purge node_modules. Block the URL at the egress proxy. Rotate any tokens that were accessible during the install. 3. Hunt: search the past 30 days of DeviceProcessEvents for any other host that resolved the same URL, audit the project's git history for the commit that introduced the dep (and the PR reviewer chain), and verify whether downstream packages in the org reference the same Git source.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm-cli.js"))
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("git+","git://","git+ssh","git+https","git+http",".tgz",".tar.gz")
| where ProcessCommandLine !contains "registry.npmjs.org"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ProcName = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where (ProcName in ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd")
     or CommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm-cli.js"))
| where CommandLine has_any ("git+","git://","git+ssh","git+https","git+http",".tgz",".tar.gz")
| where CommandLine !contains "registry.npmjs.org"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: npm install Pulling Dependency from Git or Remote URL
id: 7b9d2f4a-1c6e-4f8a-9b3d-5e7c1a2b8d03
description: Detects 'npm install' / 'npm ci' command lines that resolve a dependency from a git+ URL, git+ssh / git+https reference, or a remote https tarball — the path GitHub is closing in npm v12 behind --allow-git/--allow-remote because a Git dep's .npmrc can override the Git executable.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/github-to-disable-npm-install-scripts.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.001
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_npm:

  selection_remote:

  - CI runners pinned to upstream git refs
  - Local tarball test fixtures
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE OR *\\npm.cmd) OR @CommandLine:(*"npm install"* OR *"npm ci"* OR *npm-cli.js*)) @CommandLine:(*git+* OR *"git://"* OR *git+ssh* OR *git+https* OR *git+http* OR *.tgz OR *.tar.gz) -@CommandLine:*registry.npmjs.org*

Attempt to re-enable npm install lifecycle scripts (--no-ignore-scripts / NPM_CONFIG override) AIWeaponization High
Hunts explicit attempts to re-enable npm install-time lifecycle scripts after npm v12's opt-in default — '--ignore-scripts=false', '--no-ignore-scripts', '--allow-scripts', '--allow-git', '--allow-remote' on the command line, or NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false set on the parent. This is adversary tradecraft signalling awareness of the new defaults and an attempt to restore the install-time code-execution path GitHub closed. Rationale: Article enumerates the exact new safety flags ('--allow-git', '--allow-remote', '--ignore-scripts', 'allowScripts' behaviour, the 'npm approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending' migration path). An invocation explicitly setting any of these to permissive after npm v12 ships is adversary-aware tradecraft — the strings are vendor-specific, post-defense, and rare in legitimate workflows outside known CI hosts or package-maintainer machines.
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Package maintainer running `npm install --no-ignore-scripts` locally to test their own install hook
  • Authorized CI runner explicitly opting back into scripts via a controlled environment variable
  • Internal build automation that legitimately needs '--allow-git' against the org's private Git mirror
  • Developer reproducing an install-script bug for support / debugging
  • Documentation / tutorial steps that walk through enabling scripts
Suppression filter
and not AccountName in~ ("ci-runner","build-svc","npm-maintainer","jenkins","gh-actions-runner")
and not InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\runner\\","\\actions-runner\\","\\jenkins\\","\\gitlab-runner\\")
Response runbook
1. Triage: identify the user and host. Is the account a known package-maintainer or a sanctioned CI runner? Pull the surrounding process tree — was this a one-off invocation or did the user run it repeatedly across different projects? Check whether the same shell session also resolved a git+ or remote-URL dep (UC2). 2. Contain: if the account is not authorized to opt back into scripts, suspend the session, quarantine the project workspace, and freeze the lockfile. Verify no install-script side-effects occurred (suspicious child processes per UC1, file writes outside the project root, network egress from npm-spawned children). 3. Hunt: search the past 30 days for any other host where these exact flags ran, correlate with .npmrc file modifications that contain 'ignore-scripts=false', and review whether the same author committed package.json changes pulling in non-registry deps. Audit the CI/CD pipeline definitions (Jenkinsfiles, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI) for these flags being baked in.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm-cli.js"))
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--ignore-scripts=false","--no-ignore-scripts","--allow-scripts","--allow-git","--allow-remote")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ProcName = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where (ProcName in ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd")
     or CommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm-cli.js"))
| where CommandLine has_any ("--ignore-scripts=false","--no-ignore-scripts","--allow-scripts","--allow-git","--allow-remote","NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",

                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60

        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] CVE-2026-10520 OS command injection probes against Ivanti Sentry MICS admin port

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
