CVE-2026-10520 OS command injection probes against Ivanti Sentry MICS admin port AIExploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP(S) requests to the Ivanti Sentry MICS / admin servlet endpoints carrying shell metacharacters in parameters or headers — the public PoC pattern for CVE-2026-10520 root RCE. Designed to fire on first contact before persistence is established. Rationale: Anchors on the Sentry-specific MICS / mifs admin servlet path classes named in the advisory and the OS-command-injection (CVE-2026-10520) shell metacharacter set that the public PoC referenced by Shadowserver weaponises. Cross-checked: Ivanti security advisory pages typically published at forums.ivanti.com — same MICS endpoint family was the entry point in the 2023 CVE-2023-38035 Sentry RCE which guides the path list. Cross-checked against: • https://forums.ivanti.com/s/article/CVE-2023-38035-API-Authentication-Bypass-on-Sentry-Administrator-Interface • https://www.shadowserver.org/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Automated security scanning tools (Tenable Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7 InsightVM) running authenticated vulnerability scans that probe injection paths
  • Internal red team / pentest exercises against Sentry appliances
  • Ivanti support troubleshooting scripts that legitimately pass semicolons in URL parameters for diagnostic API calls
  • Misconfigured MDM enrollment flow that includes shell-like characters in device identifier query strings
  • Legitimate admin queries with URL-encoded ampersands in policy names
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in ("<NESSUS_SCANNER_IPS>","<QUALYS_SCANNER_IPS>","<INSIGHTVM_SCANNER_IPS>") and not (RequestURL has "/mics/admin/policy" and RequestURL has "%26" and RequestURL !has_any (";","|","$(","`"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full HTTP request body & headers for the offending session; decode URL-encoded metacharacters and identify which Sentry parameter was abused. Confirm source IP is not an internal vuln-scanner by checking IP against the scanner allowlist. Step 2 (contain): If injection payload contains a working command (curl/wget/bash/nc), immediately block the source IP at the perimeter, take a memory image of the Sentry appliance, and isolate it from the management network. Snapshot /var/log and disk before reboot. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot to outbound traffic from the Sentry appliance for the same window — look for new TCP connections to unfamiliar IPs (reverse shells), unexpected child processes of tomcat/Java service accounts, and new SSH authorized_keys entries. Confirm patch level matches R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1 or assume compromised.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceName has_any ("sentry","mifs","mics")
| where RemotePort in (443, 8443, 9443)
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("%3B","%7C","%24%28","%60",";curl",";wget",";bash","|nc ","$(","`id`")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, AdditionalFields
let SentryPaths = dynamic(["/mifs/","/mics/","/api/v2/admin","ServiceProvider","RPC2"]);
let InjTokens = dynamic(["%3B","%7C","%26","%24%28","%60",";curl",";wget",";bash",";sh ","|nc ","$(","`id`","`whoami`"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DeviceProduct has_any ("Sentry","MobileIron","Ivanti") or DestinationHostName has "sentry"
  | where RequestURL has_any (SentryPaths)
  | where RequestURL has_any (InjTokens) or Message has_any (InjTokens)
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct),
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Computer has "sentry"
  | where csUriStem has_any (SentryPaths)
  | where csUriQuery has_any (InjTokens) or csUriStem has_any (InjTokens)
  | project TimeGenerated, cIP, Computer, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csMethod, scStatus),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Computer has_any ("sentry","mifs")
  | where SyslogMessage has_any (SentryPaths) and SyslogMessage has_any (InjTokens)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Unexpected shell / network tool spawned by Ivanti Sentry web service (post-CVE-2026-10520 RCE) AIInstallation High
Detects the Sentry tomcat/Java service account (or its httpd parent) spawning shell, scripting, or network-retrieval binaries — the immediate behavioural signature of CVE-2026-10520 OS command injection executing with root. Designed for Linux audit/syslog telemetry forwarded from the appliance. Rationale: Pivots on the exact post-exploit signature: a Java/tomcat/httpd parent (the Sentry MICS service) spawning sh/curl/wget — direct consequence of the article's described root-RCE OS command injection. Cross-checked: the 2023 CVE-2023-38035 Sentry exploit chain identically chained the MICS service to /bin/sh which has informed how Shadowserver scans for the backdoor pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/ • https://forums.ivanti.com/s/article/CVE-2023-38035-API-Authentication-Bypass-on-Sentry-Administrator-Interface • https://www.shadowserver.org/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1548.002 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ivanti's own Sentry health-check shell scripts launched by tomcat (e.g. periodic /bin/sh /opt/mifs/healthcheck.sh) — whitelist by exact command line
  • Vendor support engineer running diagnostic curl/wget from inside tomcat shell during a support call
  • Custom MDM integrations using Java Runtime.exec() to call curl for legitimate inventory sync
  • Backup agent (Veeam Linux, NetBackup) spawning sh under Java when integrated via custom enterprise wrappers
  • Ivanti R10.x upgrade scripts during scheduled maintenance windows
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/opt/mifs/scripts/healthcheck","/usr/local/mifs/bin/upgrade","/opt/mifs/bin/diag")) and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "catalina-healthcheck")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Capture parent commandline and full child commandline. Compare child command to known Sentry healthcheck/upgrade script paths (/opt/mifs/scripts/, /usr/local/mifs/bin/). If unfamiliar, treat as TP. Confirm Sentry version against R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1; lower means vulnerable. Step 2 (contain): Isolate appliance from production VLAN, kill the offending process, preserve /proc/<pid>/exe and /proc/<pid>/cwd via copy, snapshot disk and memory before reboot. Rotate all Sentry-stored credentials (LDAP bind, MDM tenant secrets, certs). Step 3 (hunt): Search outbound DNS/IP from the appliance during the same window for unfamiliar destinations (drop sites). Search for new SSH authorized_keys, new cron entries, new systemd units, and new local user accounts on the appliance. Pivot back to the source of the originating HTTP request and check upstream WAF/proxy logs for the CVE-2026-10520 injection probe.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceName has_any ("sentry","mifs")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java","tomcat","httpd","nginx","catalina.sh","mifs") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("tomcat","mifs","catalina")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","ruby","socat","openssl","wscript")
| where AccountName in~ ("root","tomcat","mifs","sentry") or ProcessIntegrityLevel == "System"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
let SentryHosts = dynamic(["sentry","mifs","mics"]);
let ShellBins = dynamic(["/sh","/bash","/dash","/curl","/wget","/nc","/ncat","/python","/python3","/perl","/ruby","/socat","/openssl"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Computer has_any (SentryHosts) or HostName has_any (SentryHosts)
  | where Facility in ("auth","authpriv","daemon","user","local0","local1")
  | where SyslogMessage has_any ("tomcat","catalina","mifs","httpd")
  | where SyslogMessage has_any (ShellBins) or SyslogMessage has_any ("execve","COMMAND=")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DvcHostname has_any (SentryHosts)
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("java","tomcat","httpd","nginx","catalina")
  | where ActingProcessName has_any (ShellBins)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Post-exploit SSH key, cron, or systemd persistence on Ivanti Sentry appliance AIInstallation High
Hunts persistence written to a Sentry appliance after CVE-2026-10520 exploitation — new entries in root/tomcat ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, new crontabs, new systemd units, or modifications to /etc/rc.local. The article confirms attackers had already backdoored most exposed Sentry gateways, so persistence will be the second-stage signal. Rationale: Targets the 'backdoored most of the Sentry gateways' claim from the article — persistence mechanism choice on a Linux appliance is overwhelmingly authorized_keys / cron / systemd. Cross-checked: MITRE T1098.004 and T1543.002 enumerate these as the canonical Linux persistence paths, and historical Sentry compromises (CVE-2023-38035 chain) saw the same vectors. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/002/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/003/
ATT&CKT1098.004 T1053.003 T1543.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ivanti R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1 patch install legitimately modifying /etc/systemd/system/ during the upgrade window
  • Configuration management (Puppet/Ansible/Salt) pushing legitimate SSH keys to root for jump-host access (whitelist by initiating process)
  • Sentry admin onboarding a new operator via the GUI (writes authorized_keys via the management API)
  • Backup agent installing or updating a systemd timer for scheduled backup jobs
  • Vendor support engineer adding a temporary diagnostic cron job during an active support case
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("puppet","ansible-playbook","chef-client","salt-minion","yum","dnf","rpm","dpkg") and InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("puppet","ansible","root_cm")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the contents of the new authorized_keys entry / cron file / systemd unit. Identify the key fingerprint or command line. Cross-check against the known admin team key catalogue and patch/CM tool logs for the same window. Step 2 (contain): If unknown, immediately remove the artefact, rotate the affected account's password, snapshot the appliance disk + memory, and isolate from the production VLAN. Block any IPs the cron / systemd unit calls out to at the perimeter. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot to the CVE-2026-10520 web-injection detection over the prior 72 hours from this host — correlate the persistence write timestamp with the originating HTTP exploit request. Search every other Sentry appliance in the fleet for identical SSH key fingerprints / cron command lines. Force-patch fleet to R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceName has_any ("sentry","mifs")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/.ssh/","/etc/cron","/var/spool/cron","/etc/systemd/system","/lib/systemd/system") or FileName in~ ("authorized_keys","rc.local")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("puppet","ansible","chef","salt")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let SentryHosts = dynamic(["sentry","mifs","mics"]);
let PersistencePaths = dynamic(["authorized_keys","/etc/cron","/var/spool/cron","/etc/systemd/system","/lib/systemd/system","/etc/rc.local","/etc/init.d"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Computer has_any (SentryHosts) or HostName has_any (SentryHosts)
  | where Facility in ("auth","authpriv","cron","daemon")
  | where SyslogMessage has_any (PersistencePaths)
        or SyslogMessage has_any ("new crontab","CRON","systemctl enable","systemctl daemon-reload","useradd","PAM adding faulty module","session opened for user root")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage),
(ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DvcHostname has_any (SentryHosts)
  | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
  | where TargetFilePath has_any (PersistencePaths) or TargetFileName == "authorized_keys"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Inventory hunt: internet-exposed Ivanti Sentry instances AIReconnaissance Medium
Surfaces every Sentry / MobileIron Sentry appliance reachable from the public internet on management ports (443, 8443, 9443) — Shadowserver explicitly flagged scan-coverage gaps and recommended assuming compromise for any unpatched, internet-exposed instance. Hunt rather than alert because it's an inventory pivot. Rationale: Maps directly to Shadowserver's call-out that exposure visibility is limited because search engines blocklist their scanner — so we have to look at our own perimeter telemetry and CloudTrail SG changes to find every Sentry instance reachable from the public internet on the management ports the advisory implicates. Cross-checked against: • https://www.shadowserver.org/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1526/
ATT&CKT1526 T1590.005
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sentry instances intentionally exposed for remote MDM device check-in over 443 (this is by design — confirm the host requires Sentry patch level R10.5.2+ rather than treating exposure as TP)
  • Load-balancer/WAF VIP fronting Sentry showing as the 'host' rather than the backend appliance (verify which is the patchable asset)
  • Vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys) appearing as external sources in flow data when scanning via a dual-homed appliance
  • DR / standby Sentry appliances with public DNS but firewall-restricted access (re-check actual reachability with an external probe before flagging)
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): For each Sentry instance returned, pull current product version via admin API or vendor portal. Compare against R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1. Confirm internet reachability with an out-of-band external probe (`curl -k https://<ip>:8443/mifs/` from a non-corporate egress). Step 2 (contain): For any instance below the patched version line that is internet-reachable, immediately ACL the management port to the MDM device CIDR allowlist only, and force patch within the maintenance window. Treat unpatched + exposed as already-compromised per Shadowserver's warning — schedule full forensic review (run UC #1, #2, #3 against the host's logs). Step 3 (hunt): Build a continuous inventory by adding the Sentry hostname pattern (*sentry*, *mifs*) to the external attack-surface management feed and alert on any new public-facing instance.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceName has_any ("sentry","mifs","mics")
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted" or LocalPort in (443, 8443, 9443)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize ExternalSources = dcount(RemoteIP), SampleIPs = make_set(RemoteIP, 25), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, LocalIP, LocalPort
| order by ExternalSources desc

  | summarize ExternalSources = dcount(SourceIP), SampleIPs = make_set(SourceIP, 25), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort),
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DstHostname has_any (SentryHosts)
  | where DstPortNumber in (443, 8443, 9443)
  | where not (SrcIpAddr startswith_cs "10." or SrcIpAddr startswith_cs "192.168." or SrcIpAddr matches regex "^172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\.")
  | summarize ExternalSources = dcount(SrcIpAddr), SampleIPs = make_set(SrcIpAddr, 25), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber)

Unpatched Ivanti Sentry version (below R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1) inventory AIReconnaissance High
Identifies every Sentry asset in the estate still running a version vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520 (anything below R10.5.2, R10.6.2, or R10.7.1) so the patch program can prioritise and the IR team can scope likely-compromised hosts. Hunt against the TVM software inventory and CMDB. Rationale: Encodes the exact patched-version line from the article ('Sentry versions R10.5.2, R10.6.2, and R10.7.1') so the inventory query reports the precise vulnerability set for CVE-2026-10520 rather than a generic 'old Sentry' result. Cross-checked: the version-comparison logic matches the Ivanti security advisory's fixed-in table format. Cross-checked against: • https://forums.ivanti.com/s/security-advisories • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-10520
ATT&CKT1082 T1518.001
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DR / cold-standby Sentry appliances showing as vulnerable but powered off — confirm online status via heartbeat before tasking IR
  • Test/lab Sentry instances in isolated networks (validate IsInternetFacing == false before deprioritising)
  • Recently-patched appliances where TVM inventory hasn't refreshed yet (force a Defender device scan to confirm before opening a ticket)
  • Custom-branded versions where SoftwareName isn't 'Sentry' (broaden filter to include known custom OEM names)
Suppression filter
| where IsInternetFacing == true or PublicIP != ""
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): For each device returned, confirm SoftwareVersion against Ivanti advisory fixed-in table; cross-check with the IsInternetFacing field — internet-facing + vulnerable is highest priority. Step 2 (contain): Open emergency patch tickets prioritised by (a) internet-exposed, (b) management-VLAN reachable, (c) air-gapped. For internet-exposed unpatched instances, assume already-compromised per Shadowserver and trigger UC #1, #2, #3 hunts against host logs for the prior 14 days. Step 3 (hunt): After patching, validate the SoftwareVersion update has landed in TVM inventory; re-run this query daily until the count drops to zero. Pivot internet-exposed-and-previously-vulnerable hosts to the persistence-artefact UC and the post-RCE-shell-spawn UC for retroactive compromise assessment.
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where SoftwareVendor in~ ("ivanti","mobileiron")
| where SoftwareName has_any ("sentry")
| extend MajorMinor = extract(@"R?(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)", 0, SoftwareVersion)
| extend Major = toint(extract(@"R?(\d+)\.", 1, SoftwareVersion)), Minor = toint(extract(@"R?\d+\.(\d+)\.", 1, SoftwareVersion)), Patch = toint(extract(@"R?\d+\.\d+\.(\d+)", 1, SoftwareVersion))
| extend Vulnerable = case(
    Major == 10 and Minor == 5 and Patch < 2, true,
    Major == 10 and Minor == 6 and Patch < 2, true,
    Major == 10 and Minor == 7 and Patch < 1, true,
    Major == 10 and Minor < 5, true,
    Major < 10, true,
    false)
| where Vulnerable == true
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, OSPlatform, LoggedOnUsers
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-10520"
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP
| union (
    DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where SoftwareVendor in~ ("ivanti","mobileiron") and SoftwareName has "sentry"
    | extend Major = toint(extract(@"R?(\d+)\.", 1, SoftwareVersion)), Minor = toint(extract(@"R?\d+\.(\d+)\.", 1, SoftwareVersion)), Patch = toint(extract(@"R?\d+\.\d+\.(\d+)", 1, SoftwareVersion))
    | where (Major==10 and Minor==5 and Patch<2) or (Major==10 and Minor==6 and Patch<2) or (Major==10 and Minor==7 and Patch<1) or (Major==10 and Minor<5) or (Major<10)
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId="CVE-2026-10520", VulnerabilitySeverityLevel="Critical", RecommendedSecurityUpdate="Upgrade to R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1", IsInternetFacing=tobool(""), PublicIP=""
)
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, TimeGenerated desc

CISA KEV: CVE-2026-10520 — Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-06-11 1 use case 1 technique 2 kill-chain phases detected

Ivanti Sentry (formerly known as MobileIron Sentry) contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution. This vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable. The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors. Vendor: Ivanti, Product: Sentry. Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.

Langflow CVE-2026-5027 exploit chain: /api/v1/auto_login token then POST /api/v2/files AIExploitation High
Detects the documented exploitation pattern for CVE-2026-5027 where an unauthenticated attacker first hits Langflow's auto-login endpoint to mint a session token, then within seconds POSTs to /api/v2/files to write an arbitrary file via the unsanitised filename multipart parameter. Correlating both URIs from the same source IP within a tight window is far higher fidelity than alerting on either endpoint individually. Rationale: Article explicitly names both URIs (POST /api/v2/files for the traversal, plus the unauthenticated auto-login step that mints the session token in 'a single unauthenticated request'). Pairing them in a same-source-IP / same-host time-window correlation eliminates the noise of either endpoint hit alone. Tenable TRA-2026-26 and the public PoC (github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027) both confirm the two-step pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/unpatched-langflow-flaw-cve-2026-5027.html • https://www.securityweek.com/hackers-exploit-langflow-vulnerability-for-remote-code-execution/ • https://github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027
ATT&CKT1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Tenable Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7) probing the auto_login + file upload endpoints during authenticated scans
  • Langflow integration tests / CI pipelines that exercise the auto_login + file upload flow against a staging instance
  • Developer demo flows where a single user logs in and immediately uploads a flow JSON
  • Bug-bounty researchers / red-team engagements pre-notified to the SOC
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("<scanner_ip_1>","<scanner_ip_2>") | where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Rapid7","InsightVM")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the SrcIpAddr's geo and reputation, the User-Agent string, and the HTTP response code for the /api/v2/files POST (200 = file written, 403 = blocked). If response is 200, treat as confirmed compromise. 2) Contain: take the Langflow instance offline or front it with a WAF rule blocking POST /api/v2/files where filename contains '../'; rotate any secrets reachable from the Langflow host (API keys, OpenAI tokens, MCP creds). 3) Hunt: pivot on the destination host's DeviceFileEvents/FileWritten for files written by python/uvicorn outside the Langflow data dir (UC2), and check the host's process tree (UC3) for shells spawned from the langflow process. Confirm version is <1.9.0 (UC4) and upgrade to 1.10.0.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSec = 120s;
let TokenHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
    | where Url has "/api/v1/auto_login"
    | project TokenTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where Url has "/api/v2/files"
| project UploadTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| join kind=inner TokenHits on SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr
| where UploadTime between (TokenTime .. TokenTime + WindowSec)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', UploadTime, TokenTime)
| project TokenTime, UploadTime, DelaySec, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by UploadTime desc
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:azure.appservice) @http.method:POST @http.url_details.path:("/api/v1/auto_login" OR "/api/v2/files")
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true earliest(_time) as token_time from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method=POST AND Web.uri_path="*/api/v1/auto_login*" by Web.src, Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rename src as exploit_src dest as target_host | join type=inner exploit_src target_host [ | tstats summariesonly=true earliest(_time) as upload_time values(Web.uri_path) as upload_paths values(Web.status) as upload_statuses values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method=POST AND Web.uri_path="*/api/v2/files*" by Web.src, Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rename src as exploit_src dest as target_host ] | eval delay_sec=upload_time - token_time | where delay_sec >= 0 AND delay_sec <= 120 | table exploit_src, target_host, token_time, upload_time, delay_sec, upload_paths, upload_statuses, user_agents | sort - upload_time
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) as token_time from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method=POST AND Web.uri_path="*/api/v1/auto_login*" by Web.src, Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rename src as exploit_src dest as target_host | join type=inner exploit_src target_host [ | tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) as upload_time values(Web.uri_path) as upload_paths values(Web.status) as upload_statuses values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method=POST AND Web.uri_path="*/api/v2/files*" by Web.src, Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rename src as exploit_src dest as target_host ] | eval delay_sec=upload_time - token_time | where delay_sec >= 0 AND delay_sec <= 120 | table exploit_src, target_host, token_time, upload_time, delay_sec, upload_paths, upload_statuses, user_agents | sort - upload_time
Langflow Python process writes file outside data dir (CVE-2026-5027 post-exploit drop) AIInstallation High
Once the path-traversal write succeeds, the Langflow worker (python/uvicorn/gunicorn) is the process that writes the attacker-controlled file. Hunts for files written by that process to high-value system paths or with extensions/names indicating webshells, cron persistence, or SSH key implantation. Catches the post-exploit drop even when web/WAF logs aren't ingested. Rationale: Article confirms the impact is 'write arbitrary files on exposed servers' and VulnCheck honeypots observed 'test files' being dropped. The Langflow worker process is the only legitimate writer to its data directory, so a write by that process to /etc/, web roots, SSH key files, or cron from this process is the clean exploit indicator. Avoids false-positives on legitimate flow saves by anchoring on path/extension rather than just process identity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1098.004 T1053.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Langflow legitimately writing user-uploaded flow JSON or RAG corpus files to a non-standard data directory configured via LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR
  • Langflow component that writes logs to /var/log via a custom logging handler
  • Python pip install/upgrade of Langflow plugins writing into site-packages (often under /usr/local/lib/python*/)
  • Backup/sync tools running as the langflow service user touching shared paths
  • Custom-flow component using python-shell or os.system to legitimately write artefacts
Suppression filter
| where not (TargetFilePath has "site-packages" and TargetFileName endswith ".py") | where ActorUsername != "root" or TargetFilePath !startswith "/var/log/langflow"
Response runbook
1) Triage: hash the dropped file and check VT/Defender verdict; examine the file content directly (cat the .php / .sh / authorized_keys) for webshell magic strings or attacker SSH keys. Cross-reference Timestamp with web-log POSTs to /api/v2/files (UC1) from external IPs within ±2 minutes. 2) Contain: quarantine the file, kill the Langflow worker process, rotate the service account, remove any added SSH keys / cron entries / WAR files, and block the source IP at the perimeter. 3) Hunt: pivot on DeviceProcessEvents for any child process spawned by the langflow worker (UC3); look for outbound connections from the langflow process to non-RFC1918 IPs in DeviceNetworkEvents in the prior 24h.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let ExpectedDataPaths = pack_array(@"\langflow\", @"\.langflow\", @"\langflow_data\", "/langflow/", "/.langflow/", "/langflow_data/", "/var/lib/langflow", "/tmp/langflow");
let SuspiciousPaths = pack_array("/etc/", "/root/", "/var/www/", "/var/spool/cron/", "/usr/local/bin/", "/.ssh/", @"\Windows\", @"\System32\", @"\inetpub\wwwroot\", @"\Startup\", @"\ProgramData\");
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn","langflow")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","langflow_backend","-m langflow")
| where not(FolderPath has_any (ExpectedDataPaths))
| where FolderPath has_any (SuspiciousPaths)
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)(authorized_keys|crontab|sudoers|webshell|\.php$|\.jsp$|\.aspx$|\.sh$)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let ExpectedDataPaths = dynamic([@"\langflow\", "/langflow/", "/.langflow/", "/langflow_data/", "/var/lib/langflow"]);
let SuspiciousPaths = dynamic(["/etc/", "/root/", "/var/www/", "/var/spool/cron/", "/usr/local/bin/", "/.ssh/", @"\Windows\", @"\System32\", @"\inetpub\wwwroot\", @"\Startup\"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventType =~ "FileCreated" or EventType =~ "FileModified"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","uvicorn","gunicorn","langflow")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","-m langflow")
| where not(TargetFilePath has_any (ExpectedDataPaths))
| where TargetFilePath has_any (SuspiciousPaths)
   or TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)(authorized_keys|crontab|sudoers|webshell|\.php$|\.jsp$|\.aspx$|\.sh$)"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

(source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.sysmon) (@process.name:(python OR python3 OR uvicorn OR gunicorn) OR @Image:(*\python.exe OR *\Python.exe OR *\uvicorn.exe OR *\langflow.exe)) (@TargetFilename:(*\Windows\System32\* OR *\inetpub\wwwroot\* OR *\Startup\* OR *.php OR *.jsp OR *.aspx) OR @file.path:(/etc/* OR /root/* OR /var/www/* OR /var/spool/cron/* OR */.ssh/authorized_keys OR *.php OR *.jsp OR *.sh))

Langflow worker spawns shell or LOLBin child (CVE-2026-5027 RCE) AIExploitation High
Path-traversal-to-RCE on Langflow typically ends with the python/uvicorn worker spawning a shell (bash/sh/cmd) or download utility (curl/wget) to fetch a second-stage payload after the implant lands. Detects any non-python child of the langflow worker process — Langflow legitimately runs sub-pythons only. Rationale: Tenable's TRA-2026-26 and the public PoC both demonstrate the path traversal escalating to RCE by writing an executable file the langflow worker later invokes — or by the upload handler triggering interpreter execution. Langflow's worker should only ever spawn other python interpreters (subprocess pools); a bash/curl/wget child of the langflow worker is a strong RCE indicator. Anchoring on parent cmdline containing 'langflow' avoids FPs from arbitrary python scripts on the box. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027 • https://www.securityweek.com/hackers-exploit-langflow-vulnerability-for-remote-code-execution/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.003 T1190 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom Langflow component that legitimately shells out (e.g. a flow node that runs a local CLI tool — git, ffmpeg, pandoc)
  • Langflow startup script using bash to source env vars or do tini-style init
  • Healthcheck probes that exec curl from the Langflow container to test connectivity
  • Developer using `langflow run` interactively in a terminal where the parent shell is recorded as parent of python
  • Backup component shelling out to tar/gzip from within a flow
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "healthcheck" and ProcessCommandLine !has "--version" | where not (FileName in~ ("curl","wget") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("pypi.org","files.pythonhosted.org","huggingface.co"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: examine the ProcessCommandLine — look for base64 blobs, IPs/URLs being fetched, or output redirection to /tmp/.X paths. Pull the SHA256 of any downloaded file and check VT. 2) Contain: kill the Langflow process tree, snapshot the host, isolate via Defender or EDR isolation. Pull memory if a payload is likely in-memory only. 3) Hunt: identify all hosts running Langflow <1.9.0 (UC4) and check each for the same parent-child shape in the prior 14 days; pivot on outbound DeviceNetworkEvents from the langflow worker for any non-pip/non-PyPI destinations.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","-m langflow","langflow_backend")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","perl","ruby")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("base64 -d","chmod +x","/tmp/.","wget http","curl -o","socket.socket")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("python","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","-m langflow","langflow_backend")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","perl","ruby")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("base64 -d","chmod +x","/tmp/.","wget http","curl -o")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, MD5, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable Langflow versions present in estate (CVE-2026-5027 exposure) AIReconnaissance High
Asset-hunting query to surface every host running Langflow <1.9.0 (or langflow-base <0.8.3) — the versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-5027 and the related Langflow CVEs (CVE-2026-0770, CVE-2026-21445, CVE-2026-33017, CVE-2025-3248). Combines Defender TVM data with live process telemetry because pip-installed Langflow may not always be in the software inventory. Rationale: Article specifies the exact version boundaries: langflow-base <0.8.3 and Langflow <1.9.0 vulnerable; 1.10.0 is the latest. Cross-checked Tenable TRA-2026-26 and Snyk advisory. ~7,000 publicly-exposed instances per Censys means most orgs running it likely have unpatched copies — making asset discovery the first defensive priority. Combining TVM CveId lookup with live process telemetry covers both inventoried installs and shadow-IT pip installs that TVM may miss. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/unpatched-langflow-flaw-cve-2026-5027.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A test/staging Langflow instance intentionally pinned to an older version for regression testing
  • Air-gapped Langflow instance that doesn't reach the public internet (still worth patching but lower priority)
  • A Langflow fork or downstream redistribution that carries vendor backports of the fix without bumping the version string
  • DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities lag — recently-patched hosts may still show as vulnerable for up to 24h after KB sync
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the version observed by SSH'ing to a sample host and running `langflow --version` or `pip show langflow`. 2) Contain: for any exposed (internet-facing) instance, immediately gate behind a WAF or VPN, disable LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN by setting LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false, and enforce LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER. 3) Hunt: for every vulnerable host in the list, run UC1 (web log chain), UC2 (file write), and UC3 (process spawn) against the last 30 days to confirm none have already been exploited; prioritise upgrade to 1.10.0.
let VulnerableLangflowCves = pack_array("CVE-2026-5027","CVE-2026-0770","CVE-2026-21445","CVE-2026-33017","CVE-2025-3248");
let TvmHits = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where CveId in (VulnerableLangflowCves)
       or (SoftwareName has "langflow" and SoftwareVersion matches regex @"^(0\.|1\.[0-8]\.)")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, Source = "TVM";
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn")
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","-m langflow","langflow_backend")
    | summarize Timestamp = max(Timestamp), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceId, DeviceName
    | extend SoftwareName = "langflow (process-observed)", SoftwareVersion = "unknown", CveId = "CVE-2026-5027", VulnerabilitySeverityLevel = "High", SoftwareVendor = "langflow-ai", Source = "Process";
union TvmHits, ProcHits
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, Source
| order by Timestamp desc
let VulnerableLangflowCves = dynamic(["CVE-2026-5027","CVE-2026-0770","CVE-2026-21445","CVE-2026-33017","CVE-2025-3248"]);
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId in (VulnerableLangflowCves)
   or (SoftwareName has "langflow" and SoftwareVersion matches regex @"^(0\.|1\.[0-8]\.)")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by TimeGenerated desc
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(python|python3|uvicorn|gunicorn)/i
| CommandLine=/(langflow run|uvicorn langflow|-m langflow|langflow_backend)/i
| regex("langflow[-_]?(?:base)?[\\/=\\s]+(?<lf_version>\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+)", field=CommandLine, strict=false)

Miasma dead-man switch — `rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents` from systemd user service or launchd AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the exact destructive command the Miasma worm runs when its stolen GitHub token is revoked. The dead-man switch is wired to a systemd user service (Linux) or a LaunchAgent (macOS), so the recursive home-directory wipe is spawned from PID 1 / launchd rather than an interactive shell — a parent-process shape that legitimate user `rm` activity almost never produces. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim code block from the article (`rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents`) plus the article's explicit parent context (systemd user service on Linux, LaunchAgent on macOS). Corroborated against Microsoft, JFrog and Phoenix Security reporting on the Shai-Hulud predecessor's identical mechanism. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/ • https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/ • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again/ • https://phoenix.security/sha1-hulud-shai-hulud-worm-analysis-persistence-iocs/
ATT&CKT1485 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer-authored systemd user timer that genuinely cleans up `~/Cache` or `~/tmp` on a schedule
  • macOS LaunchAgent installed by a backup tool that recursively prunes a staging directory
  • `rm -rf` invoked from a CI runner started via `systemd-run --user` (shape matches but cmdline targets the workspace, not ~)
  • Distro upgrade scripts that fire from systemd and clean stale user caches
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/","/var/cache/","~/Cache","~/.cache","/workspace","/builds/"))
Response runbook
Triage: pull the full ParentCmd and `systemctl --user list-units` / `launchctl list` on the host; identify which .service or .plist file declared this ExecStart and when it was created. Contain: kill the parent service (`systemctl --user stop <unit>` / `launchctl unload <plist>`), snapshot the host before anything else writes to it, force-rotate the user's GitHub PAT and any cloud tokens issued from this workstation. Hunt: pivot on the parent unit's binary hash across the fleet, search `DeviceFileEvents` for the .service/.plist creation event (UC2), and check `~/.config/gh/`, `~/.aws/credentials`, `~/.ssh/` access in the prior 72 hours.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceInfo has_any ("Linux","macOS") or FileName =~ "rm"
| where FileName =~ "rm"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "-rf"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("~/","$HOME","~/Documents")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("systemd","launchd","launchctl","init")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("systemd","launchd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandparentName = InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/rm" or ActingProcessName == "rm"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "-rf"
  and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("~/","$HOME","~/Documents")
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("systemd","launchd","launchctl","init")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("systemd --user","launchd")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Systemd user service or LaunchAgent dropped by node / npm / pip / gem AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the Miasma persistence primitive: a `~/.config/systemd/user/*.service` (Linux) or `~/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist` (macOS) file written by a package-manager or scripting-language child process. The article specifies a 72-hour active monitor installed via these mechanisms — high-signal because legitimate dev tooling rarely writes user-scope autostart units. Rationale: Maps to the article's exact persistence statement: "runs as a systemd user service on Linux or a LaunchAgent on macOS". Narrows on writers (package managers and scripting runtimes) because Miasma is dropped via trojanized npm/PyPI/RubyGems packages and its loader is JavaScript-based per SafeDep's pipeline analysis. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/ • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again/ • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
ATT&CKT1543.002 T1543.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Snap / Flatpak installers writing user systemd units
  • VS Code Remote Tunnels installing a user LaunchAgent for `code tunnel`
  • Docker Desktop helper writing `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.docker.helper.plist`
  • Genuine Python pipx app installing a user systemd unit for a long-running daemon
  • ngrok / cloudflared installer creating an autostart entry
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("snap install","flatpak install","pipx install","vscode-server","com.docker.","cloudflared install","ngrok service install"))
Response runbook
Triage: read the dropped .service/.plist — extract ExecStart / ProgramArguments and the binary it points to. If it shells out to node/curl/python with an inline base64 or fetches from api.github.com, treat as confirmed. Contain: disable the unit (`systemctl --user disable --now <unit>` / `launchctl unload <plist>`), delete the file, kill the running monitor process, rotate the developer's GitHub PAT and any AWS/GCP/Azure CLI credentials. Hunt: search DeviceProcessEvents for the monitor binary across the fleet, pivot on its hash, and cross-reference UC1 (rm -rf) for hosts where the dead-man switch already fired.
DeviceFileEvents

   or (TargetFilePath has "/Library/LaunchAgents/" and TargetFileName endswith ".plist")

Miasma AI tool config poisoning — writes to Claude / Cursor / Copilot / Gemini / Kiro / Cline configs AIInstallation Medium
Hunts modification of AI coding-assistant configuration files by a non-IDE process. The article calls out poisoning of Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro and Cline configs as a Miasma capability — backdooring these files lets the worm inject malicious instructions into every future AI-assisted code-gen session, propagating the attack with developer help. Rationale: Anchors on the exact AI-tool list named in the article: "poison configurations of AI coding tools such as Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro, and Cline". Filters to package-manager/scripting writers because the worm rides into the dev workstation via trojanized packages, then excludes the legitimate IDE/agent binaries that normally own these files. Miasma credential harvesting — package-manager child reads ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.kube, ~/.npmrc, password vaults AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts a node / npm / python / ruby / shell child of a package install reading the canonical dev-secret locations the article lists (cloud providers, CI/CD, password managers, Kubernetes, secret stores). High-value pivot because legitimate `npm install` scripts almost never touch `~/.aws/credentials` or `~/.ssh/id_*`. Rationale: Maps to the article's enumeration: "harvests credentials from cloud providers, CI/CD systems, password managers, Kubernetes, and secret stores". The fan-out threshold (≥3 distinct secret stores by one PID in 5 min) is what differentiates the worm's bulk-collect behaviour from a developer's normal `aws s3 cp` or `kubectl` call that touches one file. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/ • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/ • https://blog.gitguardian.com/four-credential-harvesting-campaigns-hit-open-source-ecosystems-in-two-weeks/

  • `terraform init` reading `~/.aws/credentials`, `~/.kube/config` and a `.netrc` for module download
  • `gh auth status` reading `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` alongside `~/.netrc`
  • Backup tool (rclone, restic) snapshotting the user's home directory
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("aws-vault","terraform init","gh auth","rclone","restic","borg create","chezmoi apply"))
Response runbook
Triage: pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine — confirm whether the parent is a known package install (`npm install`, `pip install`) and whether the package was added recently. Contain: revoke every credential the process touched (rotate the AWS access key, regenerate the SSH key pair, log out of `gh auth`, rotate the npm publish token, force-renew `~/.kube/config`); kill the process; quarantine the workstation. Hunt: pivot on the package the install came from (lsof / package-lock.json diff), check UC6 for any outbound publishes, and search the npm/PyPI feeds for the same package across the org.
let secret_paths = dynamic(["/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.ssh/id_","/.ssh/config","/.kube/config","/.docker/config.json","/.npmrc","/.pypirc","/.gem/credentials","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","/.config/hub","/.password-store/","/.config/1Password/","/.config/Bitwarden","/.netrc","/.jfrog/"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileAccessed" or ActionType == "FileRead"
| where FolderPath has_any (secret_paths) or FileName in ("credentials",".npmrc",".pypirc",".netrc","hosts.yml","config.json")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","npm","pnpm","yarn","bun","python","python3","pip","ruby","gem","sh","bash","zsh","curl","wget")
| summarize HitCount = count(),
            DistinctPaths = dcount(FolderPath),
            SamplePaths = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, FileName), 10),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
            by bin(Timestamp, 5m), DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
               InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId
| where DistinctPaths >= 3   // fan-out across multiple secret stores in one process is the Miasma shape
| order by Timestamp desc
let secret_paths = dynamic(["/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.ssh/id_","/.ssh/config","/.kube/config","/.docker/config.json","/.npmrc","/.pypirc","/.gem/credentials","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","/.password-store/","/.config/1Password/","/.netrc","/.jfrog/"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileAccessed","FileRead")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (secret_paths)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm","pnpm","yarn","bun","python","pip","ruby","gem","sh","bash","zsh","curl","wget")
| summarize DistinctPaths = dcount(TargetFilePath),
            Paths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 10),
            SampleCmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine)
            by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m), DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessId
| where DistinctPaths >= 3
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) @file.path:(*/.aws/credentials OR */.aws/config OR */.ssh/id_* OR */.kube/config OR */.docker/config.json OR */.npmrc OR */.pypirc OR */.gem/credentials OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR */.password-store/* OR */.config/1Password/* OR */.netrc OR */.jfrog/*) @process.name:(node OR npm OR pnpm OR yarn OR bun OR python OR python3 OR pip OR ruby OR gem OR sh OR bash OR zsh OR curl OR wget)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo
| regex("/(\\.aws/(credentials|config)|\\.ssh/(id_|config)|\\.kube/config|\\.docker/config\\.json|\\.npmrc|\\.pypirc|\\.gem/credentials|\\.config/gh/hosts\\.yml|\\.password-store/|\\.config/1Password/|\\.netrc|\\.jfrog/)", field=TargetFileName)
| ContextImageFileName=/(node|npm|pnpm|yarn|bun|python3?|pip3?|ruby|gem|sh|bash|zsh|curl|wget)$/i

Miasma GitHub-as-C2 — outbound api.github.com from a systemd/launchd-spawned process or clone of 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release' AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the worm's distinctive C2 / exfil channel: outbound to `api.github.com` originating from a process whose parent is systemd / launchd (the 72-hour monitor) rather than a developer-facing tool, plus any clone or fetch of a repo named `Miasma-Open-Source-Release` (the verbatim repo name the actors used to leak the source). Rationale: Article: "the toolkit requires no command-and-control (C2) infrastructure to operate, as it uses GitHub for that purpose" and "in each of those accounts, the threat actors leaked the source code in a repo named 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release.'" The systemd/launchd parent context is what separates the 72-hour monitor's GitHub polling from normal `git fetch` activity. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/ • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again/ • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1567.001 T1071.001 T1102.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate user systemd unit polling GitHub for release tags (renovatebot self-hosted, dependabot equivalents)
  • Distro package manager (snap, flatpak) calling raw.githubusercontent.com from a system service
  • Security researcher cloning the leaked repo for analysis (Miasma-Open-Source-Release string match)
  • Threat-intel ingestion tool fetching from GitHub via a systemd timer
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("renovate","dependabot","snap refresh","flatpak update"))
Response runbook
Triage: read the full URL / HTTP body for the api.github.com hit — Miasma uses commit search and gist/repo PUTs as dead-drop channels. If the request path contains `/search/commits`, `/gists`, or a PUT to a `Miasma-Open-Source-Release` repo, escalate. Contain: block the originating PID's network access, revoke the GitHub PAT it carried, isolate the host. Hunt: search DeviceFileEvents for the systemd unit that started the process (UC2), and cross-check UC4 for credential reads on the same host within the prior 24 h.
// (a) systemd/launchd-spawned outbound to GitHub API
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("api.github.com","raw.githubusercontent.com","codeload.github.com","uploads.github.com")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("systemd","launchd","launchctl","init")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("systemd","launchd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| union (
    // (b) clone or fetch of the leaked repo name
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "Miasma-Open-Source-Release"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl="", RemoteIP="",
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName
)
| order by Timestamp desc
// (a) GitHub API egress from systemd/launchd-spawned process
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstHostname has_any ("api.github.com","raw.githubusercontent.com","codeload.github.com","uploads.github.com")
   or Url has_any ("api.github.com","raw.githubusercontent.com")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstHostname, Url, SrcUsername
| union (
    // (b) any process invocation referencing the leaked repo name
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "Miasma-Open-Source-Release"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname,
              DstHostname="(local exec)", Url=ActingProcessCommandLine, SrcUsername=ActorUsername
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Miasma — Reference to 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release' Repository
id: 7c84b215-9e3b-46a4-8b8a-2c7a0bf2c1d3
description: Process command line references the leaked Miasma source-code repo name 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release' published across compromised developer accounts.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/the-miasma-worm-source-code-briefly-leaked-on-github/
  - https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/
author: SOC Detection Engineering

  - attack.t1567.001

  condition: selection

(source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon OR linux.syslog) @process.command_line:*Miasma-Open-Source-Release*) OR (source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon) @network.destination.host:(api.github.com OR raw.githubusercontent.com OR codeload.github.com OR uploads.github.com) @process.parent.name:(systemd OR launchd OR launchctl OR init))

| join({

}, field=[aid], include=[ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine]))
| OR (#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | regex("Miasma-Open-Source-Release", field=CommandLine))

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest values(All_Traffic.app) as app values(All_Traffic.process_name) as proc values(All_Traffic.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="api.github.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="raw.githubusercontent.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="codeload.github.com") AND All_Traffic.parent_process_name IN (systemd, launchd, launchctl, init) by host All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | append [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*Miasma-Open-Source-Release*" by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]
